name: Postpartum Asian
summary: Warm, soft, easy food from the postpartum kitchens of China, Korea, Japan and India: ginger and sesame chicken soup, seaweed soup, congee and dal, with one-hand snacks and soups that freeze.
howItWorks:
**Warm food from four kitchens.** Ginger, sesame, soft rice and slow soups run through Chinese confinement-month cooking, Korean miyeok-guk and Indian dal. Here they are simply good, warm food: hot breakfasts, brothy dinners, and the rice wine and herbal extras left out.

**Where the hard nutrients come from.** Eggs, beef, pork, chicken and salmon carry **choline and B12**. Dairy, eggs, iodized salt and a little wakame bring iodine, and salmon and mackerel bring **DHA**, fish three times. Vitamin D and iodine run low on days without fish or seaweed, so keep taking your vitamin and your baby's vitamin D drops, and ask your care provider.

**Cook once, eat twice.** The chicken soup, salmon congee, miyeok-guk, dal and pork rib soup each make two portions, so the next day's lunch is made, and the ginger congee covers two breakfasts. On Sunday, cook brown basmati for the egg custard mornings. Big adds a third snack and bigger portions of rice, meat and tofu.

**Soups that freeze.** Divide pots into shallow containers so they cool within 2 hours. Freeze single portions without the rice, thaw in the fridge overnight (never on the counter), eat within 2 days and do not refreeze. Reheat until steaming hot (74 °C).

**Hands and heat.** Eat hot soup and sip warm drinks when baby is set down, or from a lidded mug, never over baby. Wash hands, boards and knives after raw chicken, beef, pork or fish, and do not rinse raw meat.

recipes.name: Black sesame and almond oat porridge with banana
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese black sesame porridge (zhi ma hu), made with oats for a quicker morning
recipes.about: Creamy oats cooked in milk with a little fresh ginger, then topped with toasted black sesame, almonds, walnuts and banana. It is a warm, nutty bowl that comes together in ten minutes. The **almonds and milk bring vitamin E and calcium**, alongside the oats' fibre.

ingredients.note: ripe, half mashed and half sliced

steps: Toast the black sesame seeds and almonds in a dry pan over medium heat for about 2 minutes, until they smell nutty. Tip them onto a board and crush the sesame lightly.
Put the oats, milk, ginger, cinnamon and salt in a small pot. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often so the milk doesn't catch.
Cook for about 5 minutes, until the porridge is thick and creamy, then stir in the mashed banana.
Spoon into a bowl and top with the sliced banana, the toasted sesame and almonds, and the walnuts.
recipes.tip: Toast and crush a jar of black sesame and almonds ahead of time and spoon it on straight from the jar.

recipes.name: Korean steamed egg custard with rice, shiitake and spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Korean gyeran-jjim, eaten the way it is at a family table, next to a bowl of rice
recipes.about: A silky, savoury egg custard steamed gently until completely set, served with warm rice and a quick sauté of shiitake and spinach. It is soft, easy food for a slow morning. The **eggs bring choline and B12**, and the spinach brings folate.

ingredients.note: brown basmati from your Sunday batch

steps: Wash the spinach and mushrooms. Beat the eggs well with the salt and about the same volume of water, until no streaks of white remain. Pour the mixture into a heatproof bowl through a small sieve, then stir in half of the scallion.
Set a rack or a small upturned bowl in a pot with about 2 cm of water and bring it to a gentle simmer. Cover the custard bowl loosely with foil and set it on the rack. Put the lid on the pot.

Steam on low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until the custard is completely set: the centre should not wobble, a knife should come out clean, and the centre should reach 74 °C (165 °F). Never serve it soft or runny.

While it steams, reheat the rice (thawed in the fridge overnight if it was frozen) with a splash of water and a lid, in the microwave or a pot, until it is steaming hot (74 °C). Warm the canola oil in a pan and cook the shiitake for 3 minutes, until browned. Add the spinach and cook for 1 minute, until just wilted.

Toss the spinach with the perilla oil. Drizzle the custard with the soy sauce and sesame oil, and scatter over the rest of the scallion and the sesame seeds. Serve with the rice, shiitake and spinach.
recipes.tip: On Sunday, cook enough brown basmati for the three custard mornings (a generous ½ cup raw, or about ¾ cup at Big), chill it within 1 hour, keep Monday's portion in the fridge and freeze the other two. Thaw one in the fridge the night before, use within 2 days and reheat until steaming. A pouch of cooked brown rice works too. Keep perilla oil in the fridge, use it within 2 months and never heat it. No perilla? Use sesame oil.

recipes.name: Ginger congee with tofu, spinach and egg
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese rice porridge (zhou), the everyday food of zuo yuezi, with no wine or herbs
recipes.about: Rice simmered until it falls apart into a soft, steaming porridge with fresh ginger, tofu, shiitake and spinach, with egg stirred in and crushed walnuts on top. Congee is the classic first food of a Chinese confinement month, and this pot makes two bowls so the next morning is ready. The **egg and tofu make it a protein breakfast**.
steps: Wash the spinach and mushrooms. Put the rinsed rice and the ginger in a large pot with about 8 parts water to 1 part rice by volume. Bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to a steady, gentle simmer.

Simmer partly covered for about 50 minutes, stirring every so often and scraping the bottom, until the grains have burst and the congee is thick and creamy. Add a splash of hot water if it gets too thick.
Stir in the shiitake and tofu and cook for 5 minutes, until the mushrooms are soft and the tofu is hot through.
Stir in the soy sauce, salt and spinach. Pour in the beaten egg in a thin stream, stirring gently, and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the egg has set into soft ribbons with no runny bits.
Ladle into bowls and finish with the sesame oil, scallion, white pepper and walnuts.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C).
recipes.tip: Use a cooker's keep-warm setting only if it holds above 60 °C. Otherwise cook the base the evening before, chill it in shallow containers and bring it to a boil in the morning before adding the tofu, mushrooms, spinach and egg.

recipes.name: Sesame-ginger greens with seared tofu and rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Cantonese ginger greens and Korean sigeumchi namul, on a rice bowl
recipes.about: Tender water spinach dressed in a warm ginger, garlic and toasted sesame dressing, with golden tofu and steamed brown rice. It is a quick, bright plate. The **greens and tofu bring calcium** and folate, and the sesame adds its nutty flavour.

ingredients.note: cut into short lengths and washed

steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the water spinach well, since grit hides between the stems. Cut the tofu into thick slabs. Warm the canola oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat and sear the tofu for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Boil the water spinach in a pot of water for 1 minute, until the stems are just tender and the leaves are bright green. Drain well.

Warm the sesame oil in a small pan over low heat. Add the ginger and garlic and stir for about 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned. Take off the heat and stir in the soy sauce, lemon juice and salt.
Toss the greens with the warm dressing. Serve on top of the rice with the tofu, scattered with the scallion and sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Swap in bok choy, spinach or broccoli. Whatever is crisp and green works with this dressing.

recipes.name: Ginger and sesame chicken soup
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese sesame oil chicken (ma you ji), made as a soup with no rice wine
recipes.about: A warm, fragrant pot of chicken simmered with plenty of fresh ginger, toasted sesame oil, shiitake, carrot and bok choy. The traditional confinement chicken uses rice wine; this one leaves it out, and you won't miss it, because the **ginger and sesame oil carry the aroma**. It makes two bowls and freezes well.
steps: Wash all the vegetables. Warm the sesame oil and canola oil in a soup pot over medium-low heat. Add the ginger and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until it is fragrant and just starting to turn golden at the edges. Don't let it scorch.
Add the chicken and stir for about 3 minutes, until the outside is pale. Add the shiitake, carrot and soy sauce, then enough water to cover everything by about 3 cm.

Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then turn down to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 25 minutes, until the carrot is tender and the chicken reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, with no pink inside.
Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Add the bok choy and the salt to the soup and simmer for 3 minutes, until the greens are soft. Ladle the soup over or beside the rice and finish with the white pepper and scallion.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). The soup freezes on its own for up to 3 months.
recipes.tip: Add more ginger if you love it. For the freezer, freeze the soup without the rice and cook fresh rice on the day.

recipes.name: Salmon and ginger congee with water spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Cantonese fish congee (yu pin zhou), with salmon for its omega-3 fat
recipes.about: Soft, savoury congee topped with tender flakes of salmon, fresh ginger, water spinach (ong choy) and scallion. Fish congee is a home favourite in southern China, and the salmon gives it **omega-3 fat (DHA) and vitamin D**. It makes two bowls, so tomorrow's lunch is ready.

ingredients.note: skin removed, cut into thick slices
half thinly sliced and half cut into fine matchsticks

steps: Wash the water spinach well. Put the rinsed rice and the sliced ginger in a large pot with about 8 parts water to 1 part rice by volume. Bring to a boil, then turn down to a steady simmer.
Simmer partly covered for about 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains have burst and the congee is thick and creamy. Add a splash of hot water if it tightens.
Toss the salmon with the soy sauce, the ginger matchsticks and the white pepper.
Stir the salt and water spinach into the congee and cook for 2 minutes. Lay the salmon on top, cover and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, until the fish is opaque, flakes easily and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Break the salmon into large flakes, ladle into bowls and finish with the sesame oil, scallion and sesame seeds.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C).
recipes.tip: Chill the base within 2 hours and bring it to a boil before adding the fish. No water spinach? Use bok choy or spinach.

recipes.name: Miyeok-guk, Korean seaweed soup with beef and tofu
recipes.inspiredBy: Korean miyeok-guk, the seaweed soup eaten after a birth and on birthdays
recipes.about: A clear, savoury soup of tender beef, tofu, garlic and a small amount of wakame, deepened with toasted sesame oil, with sesame spinach and rice alongside. Seaweed is very rich in iodine, so it's kept to a few grams: enough for flavour and some **iodine**, without overdoing it. It makes two bowls and freezes well.

ingredients.note: very thinly sliced against the grain
weighed dry, soaked and drained, soaking water discarded

steps: Wash the spinach well. Soak the wakame in cold water for 10 minutes, until soft and swollen to many times its size. Drain, squeeze out the water and cut it into short lengths.
Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Warm the sesame oil and canola oil in a soup pot over medium heat. Add the beef and half of the garlic and stir for 3 to 4 minutes, until the beef is browned and no pink remains.

Add the wakame and stir for 1 minute. Add the soy sauce and about 1½ cups of water for each serving. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the beef is very tender and the broth tastes rich.

Add the tofu for the last 5 minutes. Season with the salt and stir in the rest of the garlic. Meanwhile, blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, drain, squeeze and toss with the perilla oil and sesame seeds, the way Korean namul is dressed.

Serve the soup with the rice and the spinach. Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). Freeze the soup without the rice and spinach.
recipes.tip: Weigh 3 g dry per serving, not a pinch. It swells a lot in the pot. Use wakame (miyeok) only: kelp, kombu and dashima carry far more iodine. Lovely as it is, keep this soup to a couple of bowls a week. Keep perilla oil in the fridge, use it within 2 months and never heat it. No perilla? Use sesame oil.

recipes.name: Red lentil, spinach and carrot dal with ginger-cumin tadka and brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: North Indian masoor dal with a ghee tadka
recipes.about: Soft red lentils simmered with turmeric, tomato, carrot and spinach, then finished with a sizzling ghee, cumin, garlic and ginger tadka and a squeeze of lemon. Served with brown basmati rice and a spoonful of yogurt, it is comforting food that freezes beautifully. The **lentils bring iron, folate and protein**, and the lemon helps with iron.

ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the vegetables. Put the lentils, carrot, onion, tomato, turmeric and about 3 times the lentils' volume of water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils have collapsed into a soft, thick dal.
Stir in the spinach and the salt and cook for 3 minutes, until the spinach has wilted. Add a splash of hot water if the dal is too thick.

For the tadka, heat the ghee and canola oil in a small pan until shimmering. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 20 seconds, then add the garlic and ginger and cook for 30 seconds, until golden but not brown.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal and stir in the garam masala and lemon juice.
Serve with the rice and the yogurt. Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). The dal freezes for up to 3 months.
recipes.tip: Make the tadka fresh each time. It is what makes leftover dal taste new.

recipes.name: Braised mackerel with daikon and bok choy
recipes.inspiredBy: Korean godeungeo-jorim, braised mackerel with radish, with less salt and heat
recipes.about: Meaty mackerel simmered with sweet daikon, onion, ginger and a little soy and chili until the sauce clings, with bok choy laid over to steam at the end. The sauce is sweetened with grated apple instead of sugar. **Mackerel is a low-mercury oily fish**, a good source of omega-3 fat (DHA), B12 and vitamin D.

ingredients.note: peeled, thick half-moons; simmers in the sauce, no pre-boil

steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the vegetables. Spread the daikon, carrot and onion in a wide pot. Add the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, gochugaru, grated apple and about half a cup of water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, until the daikon and carrot are nearly tender.
Nestle the mackerel pieces on top and spoon the sauce over them. Cover and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish is opaque, flakes easily with a fork and reaches 70 °C (158 °F).
Lay the bok choy over the fish for the last 3 minutes, just until it turns bright green and tender.

Drizzle with the sesame oil and scatter with the scallion. Serve with the rice. If there are any leftovers, refrigerate them within 2 hours, eat them the next day and reheat until steaming hot (74 °C).
recipes.tip: Buy Atlantic mackerel or saba, never king mackerel (high mercury). Thaw frozen fillets in the fridge and cook them within 2 days.

recipes.name: Chicken and egg rice bowl (oyakodon)
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese oyakodon, with the egg cooked through and no mirin or sake
recipes.about: Tender chicken, onion and edamame simmered in a gently sweet, savoury broth, then topped with egg cooked until set and spooned over rice. Grated apple does the work of mirin here. It is a quick lunch with plenty of **protein and choline**.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.

Wash the vegetables. Warm the canola oil in a small, wide pan over medium heat and cook the onion, shiitake and ginger for 3 minutes, until soft. Add about half a cup of water, the soy sauce and the grated apple and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken, spreading it out in a single layer, and simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, until it reaches 74 °C (165 °F) in the thickest piece, with no pink. Stir in the edamame for the last 2 minutes.
Pour the beaten egg over in a thin stream, cover and cook gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until the egg is fully set with no runny parts.
Slide everything over the rice and finish with the scallion and sesame seeds.
recipes.tip: Eat it straight away. It's the one dish here that doesn't want to wait.

recipes.name: Pork rib and daikon soup
recipes.inspiredBy: Cantonese lou fo tong, the slow-simmered soup of the home kitchen
recipes.about: A clear, comforting Cantonese-style soup of pork rib meat, sweet daikon, carrot, sweet corn and ginger, simmered slowly until the pork is tender, with bok choy stirred in at the end and rice on the side. It is hands-off cooking, and the soup freezes well. The **pork adds thiamin and zinc**, and the daikon keeps the broth clean and sweet.

ingredients.note: peeled, thick coins; goes in raw, no pre-boil
kernels cut off the cob, or frozen

steps: Wash the vegetables. Put the pork in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 3 minutes, until foam rises. Drain, rinse the foam off the blanched pork and out of the pot, then wipe down the sink.
Return the pork to the clean pot with the daikon, carrot, sweet corn and ginger. Add enough water to cover by about 4 cm and bring to a boil, then skim.

Turn the heat down to a very gentle simmer, partly cover and cook for about 1½ hours, until the pork is very tender, reaches 71 °C (160 °F) and the daikon is soft. In a pressure cooker, cook for about 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Skim off any fat from the surface. Add the bok choy and the salt and simmer for 3 minutes. Finish with the sesame oil, white pepper and scallion, and serve with the rice.
Divide into shallow containers, chill within 2 hours, eat tomorrow or freeze, and reheat once until steaming hot (74 °C). The soup freezes on its own for up to 3 months.
recipes.tip: Found lotus root? Use 100 g instead of the daikon.

recipes.name: Beef and potato simmer (nikujaga)
recipes.inspiredBy: Japanese nikujaga, home-style simmered beef and potatoes
recipes.about: Thin slices of beef with potato, carrot, onion and spinach, simmered in a light soy broth sweetened with grated apple. Home-style nikujaga is made with mirin and sake; this one uses neither. The **beef brings iron, zinc and B12**, and the potato makes it a full, filling bowl.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of simmering water for about 30 minutes, until tender, then drain well and keep it covered.
Wash the vegetables. Warm the canola oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the beef and ginger and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until the beef has lost its pink colour.
Add the potato, carrot and onion and stir for 1 minute. Add the grated apple, the soy sauce and about 1 cup of water, then bring to a boil.
Turn the heat down, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the potato is tender and the beef is cooked through. Stir in the spinach for the last 2 minutes, until wilted.
Uncover and cook for 2 minutes more to thicken the broth a little. Serve in a bowl beside the rice, with any broth spooned over.
recipes.tip: Cooked a double batch? Chill it in a shallow container within 2 hours. It's even better the next day, and keeps up to 3 days or a month in the freezer. Reheat until steaming hot (74 °C).

recipes.name: Sesame, date and almond bites
recipes.about: Soft medjool dates mashed with almonds and rolled oats into sticky little balls rolled in black sesame. They are one-hand food you can eat while holding a baby. The **dates, almonds and sesame** add iron, calcium and vitamin E.
steps: Mash the dates with a fork in a bowl until you have a sticky paste.
Stir in the almonds, oats and cinnamon.
Roll into small balls with damp hands, then roll them in the black sesame and chill for 15 minutes. They keep in the fridge for 4 days.
recipes.tip: Make a batch of a dozen on Sunday and keep them in a jar in the fridge.

recipes.name: Warm tofu with ginger honey syrup
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese tofu pudding (dou hua), made with a quick ginger syrup
recipes.about: Warm cubes of tofu spooned over with a little ginger-honey syrup, black sesame and walnuts, a gentle snack in the spirit of Chinese tofu pudding (dou hua). It takes five minutes. The **tofu brings protein and calcium**.
steps: Simmer the honey, ginger and a splash of water in a small pot for 2 minutes to make a syrup.
Warm the tofu in a bowl in the microwave for about 1 minute, or in a pot of hot water, until steaming hot all the way through.
Spoon the syrup over the tofu and scatter with the sesame and walnuts. Let it cool a minute before eating.

recipes.name: Soy-simmered egg with edamame
recipes.about: A hard-cooked egg steeped in a light soy and ginger broth until it takes on a savoury, golden-brown edge, with a handful of warm shelled edamame. It's a protein-rich bite you can eat standing up. The **egg brings choline and B12**, and the edamame add folate.
steps: Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Lower the egg in gently (add a second for later in the week if you like) and boil for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk is completely set.
Cool in cold water, then peel.
Simmer the soy sauce, ginger and a few tablespoons of water for 2 minutes. Add the egg and turn it for 2 minutes, until glazed.

Warm the edamame in the microwave for about 1 minute and serve beside the egg. If you boiled a second egg, keep it in its shell in the fridge, glaze it on the day you eat it, and eat it within 3 days.

recipes.name: Warm almond and black sesame milk
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese almond and sesame drinks (xing ren zhi ma lu)
recipes.about: Milk warmed and blended with ground almonds, black sesame and a little honey, a cozy mug for when baby is down. It is inspired by the almond and sesame drinks of Chinese breakfast stalls, with **calcium from the milk** and vitamin E from the almonds.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for about 1 minute, until they smell nutty, then grind them finely with the almonds.
Warm the milk in a pot until steaming, but not boiling, then let it cool a few minutes until warm, not hot.
Whisk in the almond and sesame mixture and the honey, and sip from a lidded mug with baby set down.

recipes.name: Warm walnut and black sesame milk
recipes.inspiredBy: Chinese walnut and sesame sweet soups (he tao zhi ma hu)
recipes.about: Milk warmed and blended with ground walnuts, black sesame and a little honey, a cozy mug for when baby is down. It is inspired by the walnut and sesame sweet soups of southern China. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, and the milk brings calcium.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for about 1 minute, until they smell nutty, then grind them finely with the walnuts.
Warm the milk in a pot until steaming, but not boiling, then let it cool a few minutes until warm, not hot.
Whisk in the walnut and sesame mixture and the honey, and sip from a lidded mug with baby set down.

recipes.name: Mandarin with walnuts and almonds
recipes.about: A juicy mandarin with a handful of walnuts and almonds, a no-cook snack you can eat in the car or on the sofa. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the mandarin brings vitamin C.
steps: Wash the mandarin, then peel it and eat it with the nuts.

recipes.name: Warm edamame with sesame
recipes.about: Shelled edamame warmed through and tossed with a pinch of salt and toasted sesame. Easy finger food that takes two minutes. The **soy beans bring protein, folate and iron**.
steps: Warm the edamame in the microwave or in a pot of hot water until steaming hot, about 2 minutes, then let them cool for a minute.
Toss with the salt and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Mango almond lassi
recipes.inspiredBy: North Indian mango lassi, made lighter with Greek yogurt
recipes.about: Greek yogurt and milk blended with ripe mango, ground almonds and a pinch of cardamom into a cool, creamy drink. It's one-hand food in a glass, with **protein and calcium** from the yogurt and milk and vitamin E from the almonds.

ingredients.note: ripe, fresh or thawed from frozen

steps: Blend the yogurt, milk, mango, almonds and cardamom until smooth.
Pour into a glass and drink right away, or chill for up to a day.

recipes.name: Masala chickpeas and almonds
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Indian chana snacks and masala nuts
recipes.about: Chickpeas roasted until crisp with cumin, garam masala and lemon, tossed with a few almonds, a crunchy, savoury snack for the handbag or the nursing chair. The **chickpeas bring protein, fibre and folate**.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss the chickpeas with the oil, cumin, garam masala and salt on a tray.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the tray halfway, until golden and crisp.
Toss with the almonds and the lemon juice and let cool for 5 minutes. They are best the day they're made.

recipes.name: Apple with walnuts and almonds
recipes.about: A crisp apple with a small handful of walnuts and almonds, sweet, juicy and crunchy. It is a no-cook snack that eats well with one hand. The **walnuts bring plant omega-3 fat (ALA)**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the apple brings fibre.
steps: Wash the apple, slice it if you like and eat it with the nuts.

recipes.name: Banana walnut smoothie with black sesame
recipes.about: Milk blended with banana, walnuts and a spoonful of black sesame into a thick, creamy drink. It is easy to sip one-handed, with **calcium from the milk**, plant omega-3 fat from the walnuts and potassium from the banana.
steps: Blend everything until smooth and creamy. Black sesame can leave a few specks, which is fine.
Drink right away or chill for a few hours.

recipes.name: Yogurt with mandarin and toasted almonds
recipes.about: Thick Greek yogurt topped with juicy mandarin segments and crunchy toasted almonds. It's cool, tangy and takes a minute. The **mandarin brings vitamin C**, the almonds bring vitamin E, and the yogurt brings protein and calcium.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for about 2 minutes, until golden and fragrant. Wash the mandarin before peeling and splitting it into segments.
Spoon the yogurt into a bowl and top with the mandarin and almonds.
